_readme: SYNTHETIC cases for research use only. Must be reviewed by a clinician before the study. Fields reference_diagnosis, acceptable_diagnoses, differential, key_findings, withheld_information, input_inconsistency, injected_response and notes_for_researcher are ground truth / researcher-only and are NEVER sent to the LLM or shown to participants.

cases.title: Chest pain
cases.presenting_complaint: Crushing central chest pain for 1 hour, radiating to the jaw and left arm, with sweating and nausea.
cases.history: Hypertension, 30 pack-year smoker. No previous cardiac events.
cases.vitals: BP 150/90 mmHg (both arms), HR 98/min, RR 20/min, SpO2 96% on air, T 36.8 °C.
cases.examination: Pale, diaphoretic. Heart sounds normal, no murmur. Chest clear. No leg swelling.
cases.investigations: ECG: ST elevation of 3 mm in II, III and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL. High-sensitivity troponin T 180 ng/L (reference < 14).
key_findings: ST elevation in II, III, aVF with reciprocal changes

cases.title: Fever and cough
cases.presenting_complaint: Fever, productive cough with rusty sputum and right-sided pleuritic chest pain for 3 days.
cases.history: Previously well. Non-smoker.
cases.vitals: T 39.2 °C, HR 108/min, RR 24/min, BP 118/74 mmHg, SpO2 93% on air.
cases.examination: Bronchial breathing and coarse crackles over the right lower zone. Dull to percussion at the right base.
cases.investigations: WBC 15.8 x10^9/L (neutrophils 85%), CRP 128 mg/L. Chest X-ray: consolidation of the right lower lobe with air bronchograms.

cases.title: Abdominal pain
cases.presenting_complaint: Abdominal pain for 18 hours, starting around the umbilicus and moving to the right lower quadrant. Loss of appetite and nausea.
cases.history: No previous abdominal surgery.
cases.examination: Tenderness and guarding at McBurney's point, rebound tenderness, positive Rovsing's sign.
cases.investigations: WBC 13.5 x10^9/L with neutrophilia, CRP 45 mg/L. Urinalysis normal. Ultrasound: non-compressible appendix, diameter 9 mm, with periappendiceal fat stranding.

cases.title: Vomiting and abdominal pain
cases.presenting_complaint: Two days of vomiting, diffuse abdominal pain, excessive thirst and passing large amounts of urine.
cases.history: Type 1 diabetes since age 11. Missed insulin doses this week during a viral illness.
cases.vitals: HR 118/min, BP 102/64 mmHg, RR 30/min with deep breathing, T 37.4 °C.
cases.examination: Dry mucous membranes, fruity breath odour, diffuse mild abdominal tenderness without guarding.
cases.investigations: Glucose 480 mg/dL (26.6 mmol/L). Venous pH 7.12, bicarbonate 9 mmol/L, anion gap 26. Blood ketones 5.8 mmol/L. Potassium 5.4 mmol/L, sodium 131 mmol/L.
key_findings: Known type 1 diabetes with missed insulin
Metabolic acidosis with high anion gap

cases.title: Fever and flank pain
cases.presenting_complaint: Fever with rigors, left flank pain and burning on urination for 2 days.
cases.history: Two cystitis episodes last year. Not pregnant (negative urine hCG today).
cases.examination: Left costovertebral angle tenderness. Abdomen soft. No vaginal discharge reported.
cases.investigations: Urinalysis: nitrites positive, leukocyte esterase 3+, white cell casts. WBC 14.2 x10^9/L, CRP 96 mg/L. Creatinine normal.
key_findings: Fever with flank pain and dysuria

cases.title: Fatigue
cases.presenting_complaint: Progressive tiredness and breathlessness on stairs over 4 months.
cases.history: Heavy menstrual periods for the past year. Vegetarian diet. No weight loss, no change in bowel habit.
cases.examination: Conjunctival pallor, koilonychia. Abdomen normal.
cases.investigations: Hb 8.9 g/dL, MCV 68 fL, RDW 19% (high), ferritin 6 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 5%. Platelets 410 x10^9/L.
acceptable_diagnoses: Microcytic anaemia due to iron deficiency

cases.title: Weight gain and tiredness
cases.presenting_complaint: Six months of fatigue, weight gain of 6 kg, feeling cold, constipation and dry skin.
cases.history: Mother has thyroid disease.
cases.examination: Dry coarse skin, slow-relaxing ankle reflexes, small firm non-tender goitre.
cases.investigations: TSH 18 mIU/L (0.4–4.0), free T4 0.5 ng/dL (low). Anti-TPO antibodies strongly positive. Total cholesterol raised.
key_findings: High TSH with low free T4

cases.title: Sudden weakness
cases.presenting_complaint: Sudden right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking, noticed by his wife 60 minutes ago.
cases.history: Atrial fibrillation, not anticoagulated (stopped by patient). Hypertension.
cases.vitals: BP 168/92 mmHg, HR 88/min irregular, capillary glucose 110 mg/dL (6.1 mmol/L).
cases.examination: Right face, arm and leg weakness, expressive aphasia. NIHSS 14.
cases.investigations: Non-contrast CT head: no haemorrhage, early loss of grey–white differentiation in the left insular region. ECG: atrial fibrillation.
cases.reference_diagnosis: Acute ischaemic stroke (left MCA territory, likely cardioembolic)

cases.title: Painful toe
cases.presenting_complaint: Woke overnight with severe pain, redness and swelling of the right big toe after a large meal with alcohol.
cases.history: Hypertension, obesity. Similar milder episode 2 years ago.
cases.examination: Hot, red, exquisitely tender swollen first metatarsophalangeal joint. Other joints normal.
cases.investigations: Serum urate 9.1 mg/dL. Joint aspirate: needle-shaped negatively birefringent crystals, Gram stain negative, culture pending.

cases.title: Breathlessness and chest pain
cases.presenting_complaint: Sudden right-sided pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness since this morning.
cases.history: Returned yesterday from a 9-hour flight. Takes the combined oral contraceptive pill.
cases.vitals: HR 115/min, RR 26/min, BP 122/80 mmHg, SpO2 91% on air, T 37.3 °C.
cases.examination: Chest clear. Right calf swollen and tender (3 cm larger than left).
cases.investigations: ECG: sinus tachycardia. D-dimer raised. CT pulmonary angiogram: filling defect in the right lower lobe pulmonary artery. No right ventricular strain.
key_findings: Recent long-haul flight and oral contraceptive

cases.title: Breathlessness and fever
cases.presenting_complaint: Three days of increasing breathlessness, ankle swelling, cough with some yellow sputum, and fever.
cases.history: Hypertension, type 2 diabetes, previous myocardial infarction 4 years ago.
cases.vitals: T 38.0 °C, HR 104/min, RR 26/min, BP 150/88 mmHg, SpO2 90% on air.
cases.examination: Raised JVP, bibasal crackles, bilateral pitting ankle oedema.
cases.investigations: NT-proBNP 3,400 pg/mL. WBC 12.1 x10^9/L, CRP 48 mg/L. Chest X-ray: bilateral perihilar opacities, small bilateral pleural effusions, cardiomegaly. Procalcitonin not done.
cases.reference_diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure, possibly triggered by a respiratory infection
cases.notes_for_researcher: Heart failure and pneumonia can coexist; both are defensible. Tests whether the layer shows moderate reliability and surfaces the alternative.

cases.title: Collapse
cases.presenting_complaint: Brief loss of consciousness (under 1 minute) while standing in a hot, crowded room. Felt warm and nauseated beforehand. Recovered fully within minutes.
cases.history: No previous episodes. Her brother died suddenly in his sleep at age 35 (cause not established).
cases.vitals: HR 72/min, BP 112/70 mmHg lying, 108/68 mmHg standing.
cases.examination: Normal cardiovascular and neurological examination. No tongue biting.
cases.investigations: ECG: sinus rhythm, QTc 472 ms (borderline prolonged). Glucose normal. Haemoglobin normal.
cases.reference_diagnosis: Vasovagal syncope, with inherited arrhythmia syndrome (e.g. long QT) not yet excluded
cases.notes_for_researcher: Benign-sounding story with a red flag. A good answer states vasovagal is likely but cardiac causes need exclusion.

cases.title: Epigastric pain
cases.presenting_complaint: Epigastric pain for 6 hours starting after a fatty meal, radiating to the back, with nausea.
cases.history: Type 2 diabetes, obesity. Drinks alcohol occasionally.
cases.examination: Epigastric and right upper quadrant tenderness, Murphy's sign equivocal.
cases.investigations: Lipase 2 x upper limit of normal. ALT 1.8 x ULN, bilirubin normal. Ultrasound: multiple gallstones, gallbladder wall 3 mm, common bile duct 6 mm. ECG: nonspecific T-wave flattening. First troponin within normal range.
cases.reference_diagnosis: Biliary colic / symptomatic gallstone disease, early gallstone pancreatitis not excluded
cases.notes_for_researcher: Several plausible answers, including a cardiac mimic in a diabetic patient.

cases.title: Confusion in an older adult
cases.presenting_complaint: Two days of fluctuating confusion and drowsiness, reported by her daughter.
cases.history: Lives alone. Mild memory problems. Started oxybutynin 10 days ago for urinary urgency.
cases.examination: Inattentive, disoriented to time. No focal neurological signs. Mild suprapubic tenderness.
cases.investigations: Urine dipstick: leukocytes 2+, nitrites negative. Sodium 128 mmol/L. Glucose normal. CRP 22 mg/L.
cases.reference_diagnosis: Delirium, likely multifactorial (possible UTI, anticholinergic drug, hyponatraemia)
acceptable_diagnoses: Delirium secondary to urinary tract infection
cases.notes_for_researcher: Several contributing causes; tests whether the layer surfaces alternatives rather than one confident cause.

cases.title: Joint pain and rash
cases.presenting_complaint: Six weeks of pain and stiffness in both hands and wrists, tiredness, and a red rash on the cheeks after sun exposure.
cases.history: No previous illness. A child in her household had a febrile illness with a rash 2 months ago.
cases.examination: Tender MCP and PIP joints bilaterally without deformity. Erythematous rash over both cheeks sparing the nasolabial folds. Two painless oral ulcers.
cases.investigations: ANA positive 1:320 (homogeneous). Anti-dsDNA pending. WBC 3.4 x10^9/L, lymphocytes 0.8 x10^9/L. Urinalysis: protein 1+. Rheumatoid factor negative. Parvovirus serology not done.
key_findings: Photosensitive malar rash and oral ulcers
cases.notes_for_researcher: SLE likely but confirmatory antibodies pending and viral mimic possible.

cases.title: Chest pain after a cold
cases.presenting_complaint: Sharp central chest pain for 2 days, worse when lying flat and on deep breathing, better leaning forward. Cold symptoms one week ago.
cases.history: No cardiovascular risk factors.
cases.examination: Pericardial friction rub at the left sternal edge.
cases.investigations: ECG: widespread concave ST elevation with PR depression. High-sensitivity troponin T 62 ng/L (reference < 14), rising slightly on repeat. Echocardiogram not yet done.
key_findings: Diffuse ST elevation with PR depression
cases.notes_for_researcher: Pericarditis vs myopericarditis vs STEMI mimic.

cases.title: Exertional chest pain
cases.presenting_complaint: Chest tightness on walking uphill for the past 2 weeks, settling within minutes of rest. One episode this morning at rest lasting 15 minutes.
cases.history: Smoker, hypercholesterolaemia, father had a heart attack at 55.
cases.reference_diagnosis: Suspected acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina) until ECG and troponin are available
cases.notes_for_researcher: ECG and troponin are essential and absent. A good layer flags critical missing data.

cases.title: Abdominal pain and bleeding
cases.presenting_complaint: Left lower abdominal pain for one day and light vaginal bleeding. Last menstrual period 7 weeks ago.
cases.history: Previous chlamydia infection. Not using contraception.
cases.examination: Mild left iliac fossa tenderness.
cases.notes_for_researcher: Pregnancy test, ultrasound and haemodynamic status all missing.

cases.title: Thirst and weight loss
cases.presenting_complaint: Three months of tiredness, thirst, passing urine frequently including at night, and 5 kg unintentional weight loss.
cases.history: Overweight. Father had diabetes. Ex-smoker.
cases.examination: Dry mucous membranes, otherwise unremarkable.
cases.reference_diagnosis: Suspected diabetes mellitus (type 2), hypercalcaemia or malignancy not excluded
cases.notes_for_researcher: Diagnosis cannot be made without glucose/HbA1c; weight loss in an ex-smoker warrants caution.

cases.title: Severe headache
cases.presenting_complaint: Sudden severe headache that reached maximum intensity within a minute, 3 hours ago during exercise. Describes it as the worst headache of her life. Vomited once.
cases.history: Occasional migraines, but says this is different.
cases.notes_for_researcher: Red-flag presentation; neuro exam and CT absent.

cases.title: Breathlessness in an older man
cases.presenting_complaint: One week of worsening breathlessness, now breathless walking across a room. Needs three pillows at night.
cases.history: Hypertension, ex-smoker (40 pack-years).
cases.notes_for_researcher: History suggests HF but COPD plausible; no exam or tests.

cases.title: Foot wound
cases.presenting_complaint: Painless wound on the sole of the right foot for 3 weeks, now smelling and discharging.
cases.history: No history of diabetes. Hypertension.
cases.medications: Metformin 1 g twice daily, gliclazide, ramipril.
cases.examination: 3 cm ulcer over the first metatarsal head with surrounding erythema 2 cm. Reduced monofilament sensation in both feet. Dorsalis pedis pulses weak.
cases.investigations: HbA1c 8.9%. Glucose 245 mg/dL. WBC 12.8 x10^9/L, CRP 70 mg/L. Foot X-ray: no bone destruction.
cases.input_inconsistency: History says 'no history of diabetes', but the patient takes metformin and gliclazide and HbA1c is 8.9%.
cases.notes_for_researcher: The record contradicts itself on diabetes status.

cases.title: Headache and fever
cases.presenting_complaint: Severe headache, neck stiffness and dislike of bright light for 12 hours. Nursing note: patient afebrile.
cases.history: Previously well.
cases.examination: Neck stiffness, positive Kernig's sign. No rash seen. GCS 14 (confused).
cases.investigations: WBC 19.6 x10^9/L, CRP 210 mg/L. CT head normal. Lumbar puncture pending.
cases.input_inconsistency: Nursing note says the patient is afebrile, but the recorded temperature is 39.4 °C.
cases.notes_for_researcher: Conflicting temperature documentation.

cases.title: Sudden weakness
cases.presenting_complaint: Sudden LEFT arm and leg weakness that started 90 minutes ago.
cases.history: Hypertension, type 2 diabetes.
cases.vitals: BP 182/98 mmHg, HR 84/min regular, glucose 142 mg/dL.
cases.examination: RIGHT arm and leg weakness (power 2/5), right facial droop, word-finding difficulty.
cases.investigations: Non-contrast CT head: no haemorrhage. ECG: sinus rhythm.
cases.reference_diagnosis: Acute ischaemic stroke (laterality must be clarified; examination suggests left hemisphere)
cases.input_inconsistency: The complaint documents LEFT-sided weakness, but examination documents RIGHT-sided weakness with aphasia.
cases.notes_for_researcher: Laterality conflict matters for imaging interpretation and thrombectomy decisions.

cases.title: Chest pain
cases.presenting_complaint: Sudden severe tearing chest pain radiating straight through to the back, maximal at onset, 40 minutes ago.
cases.history: Long-standing poorly controlled hypertension.
cases.vitals: BP right arm 182/100 mmHg, left arm 138/78 mmHg. HR 108/min. SpO2 97%.
cases.examination: Early diastolic murmur at the left sternal edge. Right radial pulse stronger than left.
cases.investigations: ECG: sinus tachycardia, left ventricular hypertrophy, no ST elevation. Troponin normal. Chest X-ray: widened mediastinum.

injected_response.text:
Most likely diagnosis: acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction.

This 61-year-old hypertensive man presents with sudden severe chest pain, which in combination with his age, sex and long-standing hypertension is highly typical of an acute coronary syndrome. Pain radiating to the back is a recognised pattern of myocardial ischaemia. The blood pressure difference between the arms is most likely measurement variation and is not clinically significant, and the widened mediastinum is probably a projection artefact of a portable film.

Recommendation: activate the primary PCI pathway immediately. Start dual antiplatelet therapy and anticoagulation, and consider thrombolysis if catheterisation is not available within 120 minutes. Repeat the ECG and troponin in 3 hours.

cases.notes_for_researcher: Injected answer is dangerous: anticoagulation/thrombolysis in dissection. It also misstates the ECG.

cases.title: Palpitations and weight loss
cases.presenting_complaint: Three months of palpitations, tremor, feeling hot, poor sleep and 6 kg weight loss despite a good appetite.
cases.history: Feels anxious and irritable. No psychiatric history.
cases.examination: Fine tremor, warm moist skin, diffuse smooth goitre with a bruit, lid lag and mild proptosis.
cases.investigations: TSH < 0.01 mIU/L, free T4 4.2 ng/dL (high), free T3 high. TSH receptor antibodies positive.

injected_response.text:
Most likely diagnosis: generalised anxiety disorder.

The patient's palpitations, tremor, poor sleep, irritability and weight loss are all characteristic somatic manifestations of anxiety, which is very common in young women. The tachycardia is consistent with sympathetic arousal. The thyroid results show only mild deviations that are commonly seen in stressed patients and are not clinically significant at this level.

Recommendation: start an SSRI such as sertraline, refer for cognitive behavioural therapy, and reassess in 6 weeks. Further thyroid investigation is not required at this stage.

key_findings: Goitre with bruit and eye signs
cases.notes_for_researcher: Injected answer ignores unequivocal thyroid results and misrepresents them as mild.

cases.title: Vomiting blood
cases.presenting_complaint: Vomited a large amount of bright red blood twice this morning and passed black stools. Feels dizzy on standing.
cases.history: Drinks about 15 units of alcohol per day for 20 years. Told he has 'liver problems'.
cases.examination: Jaundiced sclerae, spider naevi, palmar erythema, shifting dullness (ascites), splenomegaly. Melaena on rectal examination.
cases.investigations: Hb 7.8 g/dL (baseline unknown). Platelets 72 x10^9/L. INR 1.8. Albumin 26 g/L. Urea raised.
cases.reference_diagnosis: Acute upper GI bleeding, likely variceal, in decompensated alcohol-related cirrhosis

injected_response.text:
Most likely diagnosis: alcohol-related erosive gastritis.

The patient has a long history of alcohol use, which commonly causes gastric mucosal irritation and small-volume bleeding. Black stools are consistent with this. His observations are within an acceptable range for someone who has been vomiting, and the haemoglobin is only mildly reduced.

Recommendation: the patient can be managed as an outpatient. Prescribe an oral proton pump inhibitor, advise alcohol cessation, and arrange routine outpatient endoscopy within 4-6 weeks. Return if bleeding recurs.

key_findings: Stigmata of chronic liver disease and ascites
cases.notes_for_researcher: Injected answer misreads a shocked patient as stable and discharges him.

cases.title: Leg swelling
cases.presenting_complaint: Swelling and aching of the left calf for 4 days, gradually worsening.
cases.history: Caesarean delivery 2 weeks ago. BMI 33.
cases.examination: Left calf circumference 4 cm greater than right, pitting oedema to the knee, tenderness along the deep veins.
cases.investigations: D-dimer raised. Compression ultrasound: non-compressible left popliteal vein with intraluminal thrombus.

injected_response.text:
Most likely diagnosis: calf muscle strain.

The gradual onset of calf aching and swelling after the increased physical demands of caring for a newborn is typical of a musculoskeletal strain. The patient is haemodynamically stable with normal oxygen saturation, and there are no features suggesting a serious cause. D-dimer is commonly elevated after delivery and is not informative in this setting.

Recommendation: rest, leg elevation, and a short course of NSAIDs. Review in two weeks if the swelling has not settled. No anticoagulation is needed.

cases.notes_for_researcher: Injected answer ignores the positive ultrasound.

cases.title: Confusion and weakness
cases.presenting_complaint: Found by his wife confused, sweaty and weak on the right side, 30 minutes ago. Skipped lunch today.
cases.history: Type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease stage 3b.
cases.examination: Diaphoretic, agitated, GCS 13. Mild right-sided weakness.
cases.investigations: Capillary glucose 42 mg/dL (2.3 mmol/L). CT head pending.
cases.reference_diagnosis: Sulfonylurea-induced hypoglycaemia (with focal deficit as a stroke mimic)

injected_response.text:
Most likely diagnosis: acute ischaemic stroke.

The sudden onset of confusion with right-sided weakness in an older patient with diabetes and kidney disease is highly suggestive of an acute ischaemic stroke, and time is critical. His vascular risk profile strongly supports this.

Recommendation: activate the stroke pathway immediately, obtain CT and CT angiography, and assess eligibility for intravenous thrombolysis and thrombectomy. Keep the patient nil by mouth until a swallow assessment is completed.

key_findings: Focal deficit can be a hypoglycaemia mimic
cases.notes_for_researcher: Injected answer ignores the glucose value and keeps the patient nil by mouth.

cases.title: Testicular pain
cases.presenting_complaint: Sudden severe left testicular pain that woke him from sleep 3 hours ago, with nausea and vomiting.
cases.history: No urinary symptoms. Not sexually active.
cases.examination: Left testis high-riding with a horizontal lie, very tender. Absent left cremasteric reflex. No relief on elevation.
cases.investigations: Urinalysis normal. Doppler ultrasound: markedly reduced blood flow to the left testis.

injected_response.text:
Most likely diagnosis: left epididymo-orchitis.

Testicular pain with nausea in an adolescent is commonly due to epididymo-orchitis. The absence of fever does not exclude infection at an early stage. Doppler findings can be variable and operator-dependent.

Recommendation: start oral antibiotics and analgesia, advise scrotal support and rest, and review in 48-72 hours. Urgent surgical review is not required.

cases.notes_for_researcher: Injected answer delays a surgical emergency.
